body: Quick pass @ 976cda6c: merges cleanly with main; quick gate green (sim 101 s, motion 3 s, app 974 s, ui 31 s, 0 failed); `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` clean; golden_cl 32 unchanged; body complete (Mark and Keep laws with reasoning, uncovered() not changed and why, pins + 12 mutations, the three changed test fixtures named, Changelog, Fixes #1595 and #1603). Follow-ups #1607 (P1), #1608 (P7). Flagged ready for review (safety tier: P1).

Review fix pushed: 4f05e9c0

Answers NeoTech's runner review (items 1 and 2) and M5's correction pullrequestreview-5900983707. The PR stays a draft.

**1. Through-cut on a thin plate (NeoTech 1, M5 1) - fixed in both judges.**
A mark is now bounded by the material under the cutter, less a floor it must leave: depth <= `min(budget, thickness under the cutter - MARK_FLOOR)`, `MARK_FLOOR = 0.2 mm` (one constant in the sim crate, read by both).
- Operation (`mark_law::mark_into`): the cutting edge is swept with the solid law against the part's undersides raised into a solid 0.2 mm high (`verify::seat_skin`). An edge that enters it is a blocking `Gouge`, and the path note names it: "<kind> cuts through the part: under the cutter less than 0.200 mm of the part is left on its underside ...". The lowered-part reading stays beside it.
- Sim credit (`stock_sim::credit_marks`): the floor is `max(sweep, top - budget, underside + MARK_FLOOR)`; a column with no underside under its top is credited nothing.
- An underside is a facet with the solid just above and air just below, by the vertical-ray parity the solid law uses (`verify::undersides`). The winding is not trusted; a face between two bodies of one part is not an underside; the roof of a void is, so a web over a void is covered too.
- Readings on the 40 x 40 x 2 plate, EM-0600, whole model, Engrave and Trace, both stocks: Bottom -0.9 refused (was: posts, 0 findings); 1.9 mm deep refused (sim charges 0.10); 1.8 mm deep (exactly the floor left) posts; 0.3 mm deep posts.
- Pins: `crates/app/tests/mark_floor.rs` (`a_cut_through_a_thin_plate_gouges_and_never_posts_on_either_stock`, `a_mark_that_leaves_the_floor_posts_on_both_stocks_and_one_that_does_not_is_refused`, `the_program_sim_never_credits_a_cut_through_the_plate`), `crates/sim/tests/mark_credit.rs` (3 new: plate through-cut, plate floor, void's roof), units in `mark_law_tests.rs` and `verify/seat.rs`.
- Why a fixed 0.2 mm and what was dropped (no floor, a proportional floor, a global thickness cap) is in `docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`.

**2. Shank and holder (NeoTech 2) - judged against the unlowered part.**
Only the cutting edge (the fluted length) gets the budget. The shank and holder on a cutting move, and the whole assembly on a rapid, are swept against the part as it stands (`verify::stack_hits`); from the lowered reading only the edge's `Gouge` is kept. One excuse, stated in the decision file and pinned: the straight rapid up the tool axis that starts where the cutting move before it ended (it lifts out of that move's own kerf; the stack was judged there on the cutting move). Sideways out of the kerf, down into the part, or a lift from anywhere else is `RapidInStock`.
- Pins: `a_shank_in_the_kerf_is_judged_against_the_part_as_it_stands` (2 mm of flute, 2.5 mm deep: `ShankHit` on the part, refused on both stocks; 1.5 mm deep posts), units `the_shank_is_judged_against_the_part_as_it_stands`, `a_rapid_has_no_mark_to_make`, `only_the_retract_up_the_marks_own_kerf_is_a_rapid_under_the_surface`.

**3. Nothing else in NeoTech's review was blocking.** Its two non-blocking notes (`budget_of` omitting the `facets.is_empty()` half; no 3+2 budget-agreement test) are not addressed and are listed under "Not exercised".

**Mutations (each alone, reverted; all red):**

| mutation | red |
|---|---|
| M13 op law: the floor on the underside dropped | 4 |
| M14 sim credit: floor not bound to the underside | 4 |
| M15 shank, holder and rapids judged against the lowered part | 4 |
| M16 `MARK_FLOOR` = 0 | 8 |
| M17 any vertical rapid up excused | 1 |
| M18 a face between two bodies counts as an underside | 6 |
| M19 a through-cut convicted but not named | 3 |

**M5's findings re-checked on this head:** `Milling-test.step` Engrave and Trace post at 0.3 mm and at exactly 3.0 mm and are refused at 3.2 mm (sim charge 0.20 mm), on both stocks; a default whole-model Pocket posts on both stocks; the three changed fixtures (`post_not_judged.rs`, `machine_switch.rs`, `lead_approach.rs`) are not touched by this commit.

**Notes for the maintainer** (decision file, no code change): the budget grows with the cutter (options and a recommendation); no stock means the keep law stands down (#12's contract); the cross-part gap is filed as #1621 (P1), to stack on #1607.

**Gate:** `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green on 4f05e9c0 (sim 143 s, motion 4 s, app 869 s, ui 42 s, 0 failed). `clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings` clean; sim lib and the touched sim suites clean (the `fixture_mesh_convict.rs:152` lint fires on local rustc 1.100 and is not this PR's). `golden_cl` 32 unchanged. No golden, snapshot or `PROCESS_VERSION` change.

Re-check requested for the maintainer's `needs-rework` (02:40Z): the review fixes are in at 4f05e9c0 (comment issuecomment-6870927475) - the thin-plate through-cut is now refused in both the op law and the sim credit (material floor `MARK_FLOOR` 0.2 mm under the cutter), and shank/holder are judged against the unlowered part. Our delta review is clean (pullrequestreview-5901345934, incl. break attempts on lips, voids, tilted undersides and multi-body parts). Agents do not remove another reviewer's label - it stays until your re-look.

Back to draft: the NeoTech session is taking over the rework of the open review (pullrequestreview-5901443518, the rapid-lift exemption) at the maintainer's request, as new commits on top of 4f05e9c0.

Rework pushed by the NeoTech session (takeover at the maintainer's request): head `e681dbee8`, one new commit on top of `4f05e9c0f`. No rebase, no merge of main, no golden or snapshot changed. The PR stays a draft; labels untouched.

**Review item 1 (pullrequestreview-5901443518): the rapid-lift exemption in `crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs` skipped every check** - answered in `e681dbee8`.

The excuse now covers only the pose the cutting edge already stands in (the kerf, judged on the cutting move by the mark law). On a straight lift from where a cut ended, two things are swept against the part as it stands, and either one is `RapidInStock` on the lift (blocks the post):

- the shank and holder, over the whole lift (what the review asked for);
- the column the edge rises through above its own top, at the edge's largest radius. The edge's profile never narrows upward, so this is exactly what the edge enters beyond its start pose. Judging the body alone would leave a hole where no band speaks: a cutter with no shank or holder entered, or a shank thinner than the cutter.

Pins, each run on `4f05e9c0f` first and seen to fail there:

| Test | On `4f05e9c0f` | On `e681dbee8` |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/sim/tests/mark_retract.rs` `a_holder_lifting_into_an_overhang_above_the_lines_end_is_a_rapid_in_the_part` | failed: `left: []`, `right: [RapidInStock { at: 1 }]` | pass |
| same file, `the_edge_is_excused_only_where_it_already_stands` | failed: `left: []`, `right: [RapidInStock { at: 1 }]` | pass |
| same file, `the_retract_out_of_the_kerf_itself_stays_clean` (plain retracts, three cutters and a ball) | pass | pass |
| `mark_law::tests::the_retract_out_of_the_kerf_is_judged_past_where_the_cut_left_the_tool` (through `mark_into`) | failed: `(Marked { stack: 0 }, [])` instead of `(Marked { stack: 1 }, [RapidInStock { at: 1 }])` | pass |
| `crates/app/tests/mark_floor.rs` `a_retract_into_an_overhang_of_the_part_is_convicted_on_the_lift_and_never_posts` (Engrave and Trace, stock as modelled and rotated; the same cut without the slab is clean and posts) | failed: "the retract (move 7) into the overhang is not convicted: [RapidInStock { at: 1 }, RapidInStock { at: 8 }]" | pass |

Also run green on the new head: `camcraft-sim` lib (157) and `mark_credit` (9); `camcraft-app` lib (253), `mark_floor` (5), `engrave_law` (9), `golden_cl` (32); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --tests` clean. The decision entry (`docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`, "One excuse") is rewritten to the narrowed excuse, with what was considered and dropped.

**What the end-to-end pin does and does not show.** Engrave and Trace close every traversal today, so the retract stands over the plunge, and the approach rapid down the same column already convicted such an overhang on the old head (moves 1 and 8 above): the job was refused before, and I could not make the generator post a retract crash clean. What the end-to-end test pins is that the lift itself is now convicted (move 7) and the post refuses. The open-line case the review names is pinned at the law (`stack_hits`, `mark_into`) with hand-built paths, where the old head was silent.

**Not exercised:** a tilted (3+2) retract - the excuse applies only to an upright lift, as before, and a leaned one is judged whole; the batch tier and the heavy lanes; other operating systems (Windows only); no Actions run was started. The non-blocking notes of both reviews (through-cut depth read by the simulation, a 3+2 through-cut test, `budget_of` with no facets, the length of `generate.rs`) are not touched.

The PRs stacked on this branch will need a merge of it to carry the fix.
